heroSummary: Bambu Lab A1 prints Bambu PLA-CF with outstanding matte surface quality up to 190 mm/s (16 mm³/s volumetric limit), but you MUST swap the stock 0.4mm Stainless Steel quick-swap nozzle for a Hardened Steel hotend assembly to avoid rapid nozzle bore erosion and clogs.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate (no glue required at 55°C)
slicerTweaks: Install the Bambu Lab A1 0.4mm (or 0.6mm) Hardened Steel Hotend and select "Hardened Steel" in the A1 device screen settings before sending the OrcaSlicer job.
Cap Filament Max Volumetric Speed at 16 mm³/s so chopped carbon fibers align smoothly through the melt zone without tearing the outer wall finish.
Increase minimum layer time to 8 seconds and keep part cooling between 80%–100% for crisp overhangs on functional brackets.
Avoid 0.08mm ultra-fine layer heights; stick to 0.16mm–0.24mm layer heights to prevent carbon fiber particle bridging inside the nozzle orifice.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Sudden mid-print under-extrusion or partial nozzle clog
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Chopped carbon fibers bunching up inside a 0.4mm nozzle at very low layer heights or excessive retraction distance.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Keep retraction distance at or below 0.6mm, maintain a minimum 0.16mm layer height, or step up to a 0.6mm Hardened Steel A1 hotend for heavy structural prints.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Dimensional drift and rough top surfaces after a few spools
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Running abrasive carbon fiber filament through the factory A1 Stainless Steel nozzle enlarges and ovalizes the orifice.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Replace the worn Stainless Steel nozzle with the official A1 Hardened Steel quick-swap hotend and re-run full flow dynamics calibration.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Brittle filament snapping in the PTFE feed tube or AMS Lite
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Moisture absorption increases stiffness and brittleness in carbon-fiber reinforced PLA.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the Bambu PLA-CF spool at 55°C for 8 hours in an active filament dryer and use smooth, wide-radius PTFE routing into the A1 toolhead.

faq.question: Can I print Bambu PLA-CF with the stock Bambu Lab A1 nozzle?
faq.answer: The stock A1 ships with a 0.4mm Stainless Steel nozzle, which will wear out prematurely when printing abrasive carbon-fiber filaments. Upgrade to the A1 0.4mm or 0.6mm Hardened Steel hotend first.

faq.question: Is Bambu PLA-CF compatible with the AMS Lite on the A1?
faq.answer: It can feed through the AMS Lite if properly dried, but abrasive carbon-fiber strands will gradually wear the plastic AMS Lite funnel entry—using dry-box direct feed or TPU funnel savers is recommended.

faq.question: What layer height works best for Bambu PLA-CF on the A1?
faq.answer: A 0.20mm layer height with a 0.42mm–0.45mm line width completely hides layer lines thanks to the matte carbon texture while preventing fiber jams.

faq.question: Does Bambu PLA-CF require an enclosure on the Bambu Lab A1?
faq.answer: No enclosure is required. Carbon fiber reinforcement actually reduces thermal shrinkage compared to standard PLA, so it prints flat on the open-frame A1 bed at 55°C.
